tasks.title: Initialize shared package with Zod schemas and TypeScript configuration
tasks.description: Create packages/shared workspace with Zod 4 schemas as single source of truth, TypeScript types, error codes (L2 Table 7), category codes (34 categories from L1 Table 12), i18n keys for shared resources only (fr/en), design tokens, computeSeverity pure function, and build with tsup to ESM/CJS. Requirements: BF02-BF05, BNF07.
tasks.details:
1. Create packages/shared/package.json with name '@secure360/shared', exports field for ESM/CJS dual build, add dependencies: zod@4, tsup, vitest.
2. Create tsconfig.json extending ../tsconfig.base.json with composite:true, outDir:dist.
3. Create src/schemas/ with Zod 4 schemas using .strict():
   - auth.schema.ts: LoginInput, VerifyTotpInput, RefreshInput, ResetPasswordInput
   - incident.schema.ts: CreateIncidentInput (categoryCode, title, description, answers {moneyLost, sharedSecret, othersAffected: 'yes'|'no'|'unknown'}, isAnonymous, optional location, optional deviceAffected, clientRequestId uuid), UpdateIncidentInput (version: int, status, severity, assignedTo, resolutionNotes), IncidentFilters
   - user.schema.ts: CreateUserInput, UpdateUserInput
   - organization.schema.ts: CreateOrgInput
   - message.schema.ts: CreateMessageInput
   - common.schema.ts: UuidParamsSchema, CursorPaginationQuerySchema (limit 1-100 default 20, cursor optional), SuccessResponseSchema ({success: true, data, message?}), ErrorResponseSchema ({success: false, error: {code, message, details?}})
4. Create src/types/ inferring types from Zod schemas: export type LoginInput = z.infer<typeof LoginInputSchema>
5. Create src/constants/error-codes.ts with L2 Table 7 codes mapped to HTTP status:
   - VALIDATION_ERROR (400), UNAUTHENTICATED (401), TOKEN_EXPIRED (401), MFA_REQUIRED (401),
   - TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED (401), FORBIDDEN (403), NOT_FOUND (404), CONFLICT (409),
   - PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (413), UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE (415), IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (409),
   - RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500), SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (503).
   Note: No tenant-specific code; other orgs' objects return NOT_FOUND.
6. Create src/constants/categories.ts: 9 groups, 34 categories with fr/en labels, default severities (L1 Table 12 + SIM swap MOB-02).
7. Create src/constants/severities.ts: LOW, MODERATE, HIGH, CRITICAL with fr/en labels.
8. Create src/utils/compute-severity.ts: pure function computeSeverity(categoryDefault: Severity, answers: {moneyLost: boolean, sharedSecret: boolean, othersAffected: 'yes'|'no'|'unknown'}): Severity implementing L1 section 7.3:
   - Start from categoryDefault
   - Each 'yes' raises one level, capped at CRITICAL
   - moneyLost=true means at least HIGH
   - 'unknown' counts as 'no'
9. Create src/i18n/: fr.json and en.json with SHARED keys only: groups, categories, severities, statuses, error codes. Screen-specific text stays in apps.
10. Create src/tokens/: colors.ts (#8F5600 Moderate text, #B34700 High text), spacing.ts, typography.ts.
11. Create src/index.ts barrel export.
12. Create tsup.config.ts for dual ESM/CJS build with type declarations.
13. Add package.json scripts: build (tsup), typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test (vitest run), test:coverage (vitest run --coverage).
14. Update root tsconfig.json references array to include packages/shared.
tasks.testStrategy:
Unit tests with Vitest:
- Validate Zod schemas accept valid input and reject invalid input (missing fields, wrong types, strict mode rejects extra props)
- Test CursorPaginationQuerySchema: limit defaults to 20, accepts 1-100, rejects <1 or >100
- Test SuccessResponseSchema and ErrorResponseSchema envelope formats
- Verify all 14 error codes exist with correct HTTP status mappings
- Verify all 34 categories exist with both fr and en labels and valid default severities
- Test computeSeverity exhaustively:
  - Base case: returns categoryDefault when all answers are 'no' or 'unknown'
  - Single yes raises one level (LOW to MODERATE, MODERATE to HIGH, HIGH to CRITICAL)
  - Multiple yes raises multiple levels, capped at CRITICAL
  - moneyLost=true with LOW default returns HIGH (floor)
  - unknown treated as no
- Verify design token values match specification (#8F5600, #B34700)
- Verify tsup build produces ESM, CJS, and .d.ts files
- Run typecheck to confirm .d.ts generation works

subtasks.title: Implement computeSeverity pure function per L1 section 7.3
subtasks.description: Create pure function that computes final incident severity based on category default and user answers, implementing the escalation rules from L1 section 7.3.
subtasks.details: Create src/utils/compute-severity.ts with: type Answers containing moneyLost boolean, sharedSecret boolean, and othersAffected as yes/no/unknown string literal type; function computeSeverity taking categoryDefault as Severity and answers as Answers, returning Severity. Algorithm: (1) Start with categoryDefault; (2) unknown in othersAffected counts as no; (3) Count yes values from moneyLost, sharedSecret, and othersAffected equals yes; (4) Raise severity by count levels, capped at CRITICAL; (5) If moneyLost equals true, ensure result is at least HIGH. Export as named export. Function must be pure with no side effects.
subtasks.testStrategy: Exhaustive unit tests: categoryDefault=LOW with all no/unknown returns LOW; categoryDefault=LOW with one yes returns MODERATE; categoryDefault=LOW with two yes returns HIGH; categoryDefault=LOW with three yes returns CRITICAL; categoryDefault=HIGH with one yes returns CRITICAL; categoryDefault=CRITICAL with any yes returns CRITICAL (cap); moneyLost=true with categoryDefault=LOW returns at least HIGH; unknown treated as no in othersAffected.

tasks.title: Configure Docker Compose for PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 8 development environment
tasks.description: Create Docker Compose configuration for local development with PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 8, including volume persistence and health checks. Requirements: Technical Architecture, Phase S5.
tasks.details:
1. Create infra/docker-compose.dev.yml:
   ```yaml
   services:
     postgres:
       image: postgres:16-alpine
       environment:
         POSTGRES_DB: secure360
         POSTGRES_USER: secure360
         POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/db_password
       volumes:
         - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
         - ./init-db:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d
       ports: ['5432:5432']
       healthcheck:
         test: pg_isready -U secure360
         interval: 5s
     redis:
       image: redis:8-alpine
       command: redis-server --appendonly yes
       volumes:
         - redisdata:/data
       ports: ['6379:6379']
       healthcheck:
         test: redis-cli ping
   volumes:
     pgdata:
     redisdata:
   secrets:
     db_password:
       file: ./secrets/db_password.txt
   ```
2. Create infra/secrets/db_password.txt with placeholder (git-ignored).
3. Create infra/init-db/01-roles.sql for creating database roles (s360_owner, s360_app, s360_worker, s360_metrics).
4. Add npm script 'docker:dev': 'docker compose -f infra/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d'.
5. Create .env.example with DATABASE_URL and REDIS_URL templates.
tasks.testStrategy: Run docker:dev and verify both containers start with healthy status; verify PostgreSQL accepts connections on localhost:5432; verify Redis accepts connections on localhost:6379; verify database roles are created.
tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down this task with a focus on configure docker compose for postgresql 16 and redis 8 development environment.

tasks.title: Implement Prisma schema with complete L2 data model and RLS policies
tasks.description: Create Prisma schema for all entities (organizations, users, incidents, etc.) with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies, forced RLS, database role grants, and CHECK constraints for enum-like fields. Requirements: Technical Architecture, Phase S5, BNF19.
tasks.details:
1. Install prisma, @prisma/client in apps/api.
2. Create apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma with all models:
   - Organization: id (uuid), name, slug, is_active, created_at, updated_at
   - User: id, organization_id, email, password_hash, first_name, last_name, role (enum), totp_secret (encrypted), totp_enabled, session_version, must_change_password, is_active, created_at
   - Incident: id, organization_id, reporter_id, reference (SFC-YYYY-NNNNNN), category_code, severity (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL), title, description, is_anonymous, status (NEW/ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED/CLOSED), assigned_to_id, **version (integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, for optimistic concurrency control)**, resolved_at, closed_at, deleted_at, created_at, updated_at
   - IncidentCategory: code (PK), group_code, label_fr, label_en, default_severity (with CHECK constraint), sort_order
   - IncidentStatusHistory: id, incident_id, from_status, to_status, changed_by_id, comment, created_at
   - IncidentMessage: id, incident_id, sender_id, body, is_internal, created_at
   - Attachment: id, incident_id, message_id, file_key, encryption_iv, original_name, mime_type, size_bytes, created_at
   - Notification: id, user_id, incident_id, type, title_key, body_key, read_at, created_at
   - AuditLog: id, organization_id, user_id, event, entity_type, entity_id, old_data, new_data, ip_address, user_agent, created_at
   - RefreshToken: id, user_id, token_hash, family_id, expires_at, revoked_at, created_at
   - PasswordResetToken: id, user_id, token_hash, expires_at, used_at, created_at

   - Defence-in-depth CHECK constraint on incident_categories.default_severity (security review M1):
     ```sql
     ALTER TABLE incident_categories
       ADD CONSTRAINT chk_incident_categories_default_severity
       CHECK (default_severity IN ('LOW', 'MEDIUM', 'HIGH', 'CRITICAL'));
     ```
     This ensures that only valid severity values matching SEVERITIES from packages/shared/src/constants/severities.ts can be stored, complementing the runtime validation in computeSeverity() (packages/shared/src/utils/compute-severity.ts:9-12) which throws RangeError for invalid values.

tasks.description: Implement automated backup job with off-host storage and verified restore procedure. Requirements: O4, Phase S12.
tasks.details:
1. Create infra/backup/scripts/backup.sh:
   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -euo pipefail
   
   TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
   BACKUP_FILE="secure360_${TIMESTAMP}.sql.gz"
   
   # Dump database
   pg_dump -h postgres -U secure360 secure360 | gzip > /backups/${BACKUP_FILE}
   
   # Upload to off-host storage (within Cameroon)
   rclone copy /backups/${BACKUP_FILE} remote:secure360-backups/
   
   # Cleanup old backups (keep 30 days)
   find /backups -name '*.sql.gz' -mtime +30 -delete
   rclone delete remote:secure360-backups/ --min-age 30d
   
   # Verify backup integrity
   gunzip -t /backups/${BACKUP_FILE}
   
   echo "Backup completed: ${BACKUP_FILE}"
   ```
2. Create infra/backup/scripts/restore.sh:
   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   BACKUP_FILE=$1
   
   # Stop API and worker
   docker compose stop api worker
   
   # Restore database
   gunzip -c ${BACKUP_FILE} | psql -h postgres -U secure360 secure360
   
   # Restart services
   docker compose start api worker
   ```

tasks.title: Benchmark Prisma interactive transaction overhead and tune connection pool
tasks.description: Execute spike O8: measure the latency overhead of using one Prisma interactive transaction per tenant-scoped request under load, benchmark with autocannon at ~50 RPS, record p95 latency and connection pool metrics, then tune pool size within the max_connections 60 budget and document findings.
tasks.details:
## 1. Prerequisites
Ensure Task 8 (withTenant middleware with Prisma interactive transactions) and Task 4 (Prisma schema with RLS) are complete and working. The benchmark requires a representative list endpoint that uses the tenant context middleware.

## 2. Install Benchmarking Tools
```bash
# In apps/api
npm install -D autocannon clinic
```
- `autocannon`: HTTP benchmarking tool (MIT license, ~200 KB)
- `clinic`: Node.js performance profiling (optional, for deeper analysis)

## 3. Create Benchmark Endpoint
Create a minimal list endpoint (e.g., GET /v1/incidents with pagination) that:
- Passes through auth middleware (use a pre-generated valid JWT)
- Uses withTenant() to set RLS context via interactive transaction
- Executes a simple Prisma query with tenant isolation

## 4. Configure Connection Pool Variations
Create test configurations in apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma or via DATABASE_URL:
```
# L2 Table 20 budget: max_connections = 60 total
# Split: s360_app (API) ~40, s360_worker ~15, s360_metrics ~5

# Test configurations for s360_app pool:
# Baseline: connection_limit=10
# Test 1: connection_limit=15
# Test 2: connection_limit=20
# Test 3: connection_limit=25
```

Add Prisma connection pool settings:
```typescript
// datasources.db.url with ?connection_limit=N&pool_timeout=10
```

## 5. Run Benchmark Script
Create scripts/benchmark-tx-overhead.ts:
```typescript
import autocannon from 'autocannon';

const config = {
  url: 'http://localhost:3000/v1/incidents?limit=20',
  connections: 10,       // concurrent connections
  pipelining: 1,         // no pipelining
  duration: 60,          // 60 seconds
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.BENCH_JWT}`,
  },
};

// Target ~50 RPS
autocannon(config, (err, result) => {
  console.log('p50 latency:', result.latency.p50);
  console.log('p95 latency:', result.latency.p95);
  console.log('p99 latency:', result.latency.p99);
  console.log('requests/sec:', result.requests.average);
  console.log('errors:', result.errors);
});
```

## 6. Monitor Connection Pool Usage
During benchmarks, monitor PostgreSQL connection usage:
```sql
-- Active connections by role
SELECT usename, state, count(*)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname = 'secure360'
GROUP BY usename, state;

-- Connection wait events
SELECT wait_event_type, wait_event, count(*)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname = 'secure360' AND state = 'active'
GROUP BY wait_event_type, wait_event;
```

Add Prisma metrics logging:
```typescript
import { createPrismaQueryEventHandler } from '@prisma/instrumentation';
// Log query durations and pool wait times
```

## 7. Collect Metrics
For each pool size configuration, record:
- **p50, p95, p99 latency** (ms)
- **Throughput** (requests/sec achieved)
- **Error rate** (connection timeouts, pool exhaustion)
- **Avg concurrent connections** (from pg_stat_activity)
- **Pool wait time** (if Prisma metrics available)

## 8. Analyze Results
Compare overhead of interactive transaction vs. baseline:
- If p95 > 200ms under 50 RPS, investigate connection pool exhaustion
- If pool wait times are high, increase connection_limit
- Ensure total connections stay within 60 budget across all roles

## 9. Document Decision in docs/decisions/
Create docs/decisions/ADR-O8-prisma-tx-overhead.md:
```markdown
# ADR-O8: Prisma Interactive Transaction Overhead

## Status
Accepted

## Context
L2 architecture specifies one interactive Prisma transaction per tenant-scoped
request to set RLS context via set_config(). Need to verify this does not
introduce unacceptable latency overhead under production load.

## Decision
[Results from benchmark]
- Pool size set to: N connections for s360_app
- Measured p95 latency: Xms at 50 RPS
- Connection utilization: Y%

## Consequences
[Document any trade-offs, tuning recommendations, or follow-up actions]
```

## 10. Update Configuration
Based on findings, update:
- Prisma connection pool settings in DATABASE_URL
- Docker Compose PostgreSQL max_connections if needed
- Add connection pool metrics to Prometheus (Task 32)

## 3. Push Notification Latency Testing (BNF14)

### 3.1 End-to-End Latency Measurement
```typescript
// Create tests/performance/push-latency.test.ts
interface LatencyMeasurement {
  eventTimestamp: number;      // Server event creation time
  fcmSendTimestamp: number;    // FCM API call time
  deviceReceiveTimestamp: number; // onMessage callback time
  totalLatency: number;
}

// Server-side: Add timestamp to push job data
const enqueuePushNotification = async (data: PushData) => {
  await pushQueue.add('notify.push', {
    ...data,
    _perf_enqueued_at: Date.now()
  });
};

// Mobile-side: Record receive time
messaging().onMessage(async (remoteMessage) => {
  const receiveTime = Date.now();
  const sendTime = remoteMessage.data?._perf_sent_at;
  const latency = receiveTime - parseInt(sendTime, 10);
  console.log(`[PERF] Push latency: ${latency}ms`);
});
```

### 3.2 Test Procedure
1. Trigger notification from web dashboard (assign incident, send message)
2. Record server timestamp when outbox event created
3. Record timestamp when FCM send completes (in push.consumer.ts)
4. Record timestamp when mobile app receives notification
5. Calculate total latency: device_receive - server_event_created

**Target**: < 5000ms end-to-end (server to device)

### 3.3 Measurement Points
- `T0`: Outbox event inserted (server)
- `T1`: BullMQ job processed, FCM API called (worker)
- `T2`: FCM acknowledgement received (worker)
- `T3`: `messaging().onMessage` triggered (mobile)
- **Latency** = `T3 - T0`

Run 20 measurements, record: min, max, median, p95

## 4. System Usability Scale (SUS) Testing (BNF13)

### 4.1 Participant Selection

- 2-3 Aimé-type users (non-technical employees, various age groups)

```
Scale: 1 (Strongly Disagree) to 5 (Strongly Agree)
```

### 4.3 Test Tasks (Before Questionnaire)
Have each participant complete these tasks:
1. Login and complete 2FA setup
2. Report an incident (phishing email category, moderate severity)

4. View incident status and timeline

### 4.4 SUS Score Calculation
```typescript
// Create docs/testing/sus-calculator.ts
const calculateSUS = (responses: number[]): number => {
  // For odd questions (1,3,5,7,9): score = response - 1
  // For even questions (2,4,6,8,10): score = 5 - response
  let totalScore = 0;
  
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    if (i % 2 === 0) {
      totalScore += responses[i] - 1;
    } else {
      totalScore += 5 - responses[i];
    }
  }
  
  return totalScore * 2.5; // Scale to 0-100
};

// Target: > 70 (above average usability)
// 68 = average; 80+ = excellent
```
